title: A closing boundary leaves the subject present

source.creator: John Knopf (@johnknopf), original poster; shared by Phil Trubey (@PTrubey)
source.title: All the Way Here

motion.summary: A thin rectangular window initially frames a particle form over image texture. The rectangle contracts across successive frames while the central form remains larger and visible; the background depiction also recedes.
phases: A broad window encloses the central subject and textured background.
The boundary steadily contracts while the subject keeps its presence.
The shrinking rectangle becomes smaller than the subject.
The persistent subject becomes the visual resolution.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Animate the container and the contained subject independently to express that a person, memory or idea survives the disappearance of a boundary.
variations: A new doorway narrows while light or words remain outside it.
A map border recedes while a new river or path continues through the composition.
Use separation between an original frame and subject to express release without recreating a browser window.
cautions: Avoid copying the source window, particle form or composition.
The boundary must have a narrative role before its removal; an arbitrary box adds decoration.
Use only once near a meaningful turn, and protect the subject from cropping as the boundary shrinks.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: Relative motion communicates the idea without needing a new object or a literal illustration.
The subject remains an anchor as the amount of framing decreases.
limitations: The background and particle texture can be busy; simplified source-specific artwork may read better.
This is a sampled closing sequence, not evidence for a particular implementation or easing curve.
